title: John Terry ‘worried’ for Chelsea after Liam Rosenior exit: ‘I’ve not had a call or a message’
content:
John Terry says he is worried about the future of Chelsea following the sacking of Liam Rosenior and cast doubt on the club’s ability to attract a “top manager”.

The 45-year-old former Chelsea captain, who said earlier this season it was his “dream” to manage the club, added he “has not had a call” about forming part of interim coach Calum McFarlane’s backroom staff.

Terry won five Premier League titles and the 2012 Champions League across 19 seasons as a player at Stamford Bridge.

“I sit here worrying tonight about what is going to happen with our football club,” Terry said in a social media video on Wednesday, following Rosenior’s exit.

“Looking at us needing a manager after the weekend, I’m not sure when ownership are going to make a decision and bring a new manager in.

“Is a real top manager going to come to Chelsea football club at the moment in the position we are in? Can’t buy players, looking like we are going to have to sell potentially and that will be our best players, which is always tough.

“We will not be playing in European football, I hope I am wrong. Really, really frustrated and worried more importantly. I feel the anger, feel the frustration of the Chelsea supporters.”

Terry has a part-time mentoring role in Chelsea’s academy, which includes working with the club’s under-21 and under-18 players.

The former centre-back previously told YouTube channel Golf Life he was “frustrated” not to form part of McFarlane’s staff overseeing the first-team for January’s games against Manchester City and Fulham following the sacking of Enzo Maresca.

Terry said of McFarlane’s January stint in charge: “I feel like I should have been part of that.”

On Wednesday, the former England captain said he “had not had a call and not had a message” and that the situation would be different this time.

“I will be continuing my role in the academy, I will be in the academy tomorrow, a big couple of games coming up,” Terry said. “We will all get behind Calum, he did a great job away against Man(chester) City previously and we will get behind the boys because that is what we do.”

Tuesday’s defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion made it five straight Premier League defeats for Chelsea without a goal scored, which last happened to the club in 1912. They are eighth in the league, seven points off Liverpool in the final Champions League spot.

McFarlane’s first game in charge will be Sunday’s FA Cup semi-final against Leeds United before league games against Nottingham Forest, Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland.
